title: X-ray tube: the short-wavelength limit
caption: The bremsstrahlung spectrum of a tube is continuous but has a sharp short-wavelength limit λ_min = hc/eV (Duane–Hunt). At 50 kV, λ_min = 1240 eV nm/50 000 eV = 0.025 nm; at 30 kV it is 0.041 nm. A higher voltage moves the limit to shorter wavelength and raises the whole curve. (Characteristic lines of the target are not drawn.)
alt: Graph of relative X-ray intensity against wavelength from 0 to 0.3 nanometres: two curves that start at zero at 0.025 nm (50 kV) and 0.041 nm (30 kV), rise to a peak and fall away, the 50 kV curve higher and starting further left.
description: The horizontal axis is wavelength in nanometres; the vertical axis is relative intensity (arbitrary units).
Each curve is a continuous spectrum that is zero below its limit: 50 kV gives λ_min = 1240/50 000 = 0.025 nm and 30 kV gives 0.041 nm.
Above the limit the intensity rises steeply to a peak at twice λ_min and then falls off.
Raising the tube voltage moves λ_min to shorter wavelength and increases the intensity.
